text:
Connor Dewar has 5 points in 17 games, and the more useful number is this: Pittsburgh takes 59% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice at five on five, eight and a half points better than without him. For a 13-minute checking forward, that's excellent.

His finishing is a little behind (2 goals on 2.46 expected) and his own chances have dipped over his last ten games, 1.0 individual expected goals against a usual 1.7. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking from last season shows a dump-and-chase player: he carries the puck in on only 23% of his entries, so his line wins by forechecking.

Evolving-Hockey had him 42nd among 401 forwards last season, 2.2 wins above replacement, with a warning that the results ran ahead of the chances. That fits a player who scored 14 goals last year and has a more modest pace now. He's 27, a 2018 third-round pick of Minnesota, with stops in Toronto before Pittsburgh. We project about 14 goals. On a Penguins team that has lost a lot of games lately, his line is one of the reasons the losses aren't worse.
headline: Dewar's line is winning
